title: How Memories Become Records
subtitle: HY6101 Seminar 11 & 12 | Reading Reflection on Moments of Silence

paragraphs.chinese: 阅读《Moments of Silence》时，我一直在想：记忆的沉默一定会导致历史的沉默吗？一个人没有说出的经历，可能仍留在照片、文件或其他人的记忆里；但即使这些材料都存在，也未必能进入公共讨论。因此，我更关心的是，个人经历在什么条件下能够被记录，又会因为什么而没有被记录。Thongchai对“未能忘却”（unforgetting）的讨论，让我更想弄清楚，记忆怎样成为记录。这里面带有主观色彩的地方很多：不同的人在意什么、愿意说出什么，都会影响后来留下的记录。
paragraphs.english: While reading Moments of Silence, I kept wondering: does silence in memory necessarily lead to silence in history? Experiences that a person has not spoken about may still remain in photographs, documents or other people's memories. Yet even when these materials exist, they may not enter public discussion. I am therefore more concerned with the conditions under which personal experiences can be recorded, and with what may prevent them from being recorded. Thongchai's discussion of “unforgetting” makes me want to understand more clearly how memories become records. Many choices in this process are subjective: what different people care about and what they are willing to say will affect the records that are left behind.

paragraphs.chinese: 课堂上，老师区分了历史事实的沉默与事实所含意义的沉默。这个区别让我想到，即使知道一件事发生过，人们也未必愿意承认它意味着什么。书中1996年的纪念活动，让屠杀和暴力得到更多公开讨论，但谁实施了暴力、为什么实施，仍受到限制。〔1〕纪念打开了讨论的空间，但人们能继续说到哪一步？承认有人受害，和承认谁应当负责，是不同的事情。对国家而言，承认到什么程度，又在哪些地方保持沉默，本身就会影响这件事以后怎样被记住。
paragraphs.english: In class, the teacher distinguished between silence about historical facts and silence about their implications. This distinction made me think that knowing an event happened does not necessarily mean being willing to acknowledge what it means. The 1996 commemoration discussed in the book allowed more public discussion of the massacre and its violence. But discussion of who carried out the violence, and why, remained restricted.〔1〕 Commemoration opened up space for discussion, but how far could people go? Acknowledging that people suffered and acknowledging who was responsible are different things. How much the state acknowledges, and where it remains silent, will affect how the event is remembered later.

paragraphs.chinese: 我对记忆的“时间政治”记忆比较深刻。我认为，时间会改变记忆，也会塑造记忆。人的处境和看问题的立场变了，即使没有发现新的材料，对同一段经历的理解也可能不同。不过，我觉得政治事件对记忆的影响，在记忆产生的时候就已经发挥作用：社会事件会制造关注点和记忆点，也会塑造人的态度。书中屠杀尚未结束便出现的广播叙述，就已经开始为此后的集体记忆提供框架。〔2〕公共媒体和社交媒体的作用也让我很在意。对于未曾参与事件、原本也不了解事件的人，报道和传播会引导他们形成特定的关注点，影响他们以后怎样理解和记住这件事。
paragraphs.english: The “chronopolitics” of memory left a strong impression on me. I think time both changes and shapes memory. When people's circumstances and perspectives change, they may understand the same experience differently, even without new evidence. But I think political events already affect memory when it first forms. Social events draw attention to certain things, make some details memorable and shape people's attitudes. The accounts broadcast before the massacre had even ended were already providing a framework for later collective memory.〔2〕 The role of public media and social media also matters to me. For people who did not take part in an event and knew little about it, reporting and the spread of information can direct their attention to particular things. This affects how they later understand and remember the event.

paragraphs.chinese: 这样想下去，我很难把集体记忆看成个人经历的简单集合。政治力量和社会环境，也在影响个人怎样理解、回忆和讲述自己的经历。我并不认为，个人记忆脱离了社会主流关注，就是“无意义”的；但我也不否认，得到集体记忆的认可之后，它确实更容易被记录、被使用。难的地方也在这里：如果个人记忆在意的事情，与集体记忆在意的事情不一样，档案又该怎样记录？为了让一种经验更容易被理解，就需要把它放进大家熟悉的说法里吗？如果这样做改变了当事人原本想表达的意思，那么即使留下了记录，有些内容也可能还是没有被听见。
paragraphs.english: Thinking about this, I find it hard to see collective memory as simply a collection of personal experiences. Political forces and social conditions also affect how individuals understand, recall and describe their experiences. I do not think a personal memory is “meaningless” just because it falls outside mainstream concerns. But I also accept that once it is recognized as part of collective memory, it is more easily recorded and used. This is also where the difficulty lies: if personal and collective memories focus on different things, how should archives record them? Must an experience be described in familiar terms to make it easier to understand? If this changes what the person originally wanted to express, some of what they meant may still go unheard, even if a record exists.

paragraphs.chinese: 我还在想，官方记录会怎样描述民众记忆中那些难以公开说出的事情。书中的大赦法案受到屠杀事件的影响，却在表述上回避屠杀本身，这一点尤其让我在意。对事件的称谓也能反映不同的态度。1973年十月起义被称为“大悲痛之日”或“大欢欣之日”，就分别强调了暴力与死亡、政治结果。〔3〕我因此觉得，不能只问官方有没有留下文件，还要看文件把什么写了进去，又怎样描述它。普通人的记忆，以及那些不容易说出的经历，会不会也受到官方描述中回避和遗漏之处的影响？这个问题我还没有想清楚。
paragraphs.english: I am also wondering how official records describe events that ordinary people remember but find difficult to discuss in public. The amnesty bill discussed in the book was influenced by the massacre, yet its wording avoided mentioning the massacre itself. This stands out to me. The names given to events can also reflect different attitudes. Calling the October 1973 uprising the “Day of Extreme Grief” emphasized violence and death, while calling it the “Day of Extreme Joy” emphasized the political outcome.〔3〕 I therefore think we should ask more than whether official documents exist. We also need to examine what the documents included and how they described it. Could what official accounts avoid or leave out also affect ordinary people's memories and their accounts of experiences that are difficult to express? I have not yet worked out an answer to this question.

paragraphs.chinese: 另一方面，历史真相没有被弄清，也不一定是因为没有留下记录。有时候，相关记录其实存在，只是整理、辨认和关联出了问题。书中乍鲁蓬遗体的辨认就是这样：尸检报告和照片都在，但几份报告的页面与照片顺序错置，给辨认造成了误导。〔4〕这让我觉得，历史学家的立场也会影响研究：他是否把两份材料联系起来、是否觉得某个细节值得继续查，都影响最后能够知道什么。而如果后来的人一直沿用错误的身份、分类或描述，它们也会影响对当事人经历的理解。
paragraphs.english: On the other hand, when the truth about the past is unclear, missing records are not always the reason. Sometimes the relevant records exist, but there are problems with how they are organized, identified and connected. This was the case with the identification of Jaruphong's body in the book. The autopsy reports and photographs existed, but pages and photographs from several reports were in the wrong order, which misled those trying to identify him.〔4〕 This makes me think that a historian's perspective also affects research. Whether historians connect two sources, or think a detail deserves further investigation, affects what can eventually be known. If people later continue to rely on incorrect identifications, categories or descriptions, these will also affect how the experiences of those involved are understood.

paragraphs.chinese: 课堂小组讨论的第二个问题是：历史学家应如何研究既有历史知识的意义与限制？我的看法是，很难仅靠采访那个时代的人，就解决这个问题。首先，时间改变了思考的立场。历史学家在访问前准备的问题，可能并不是受访者认为重要的问题；即使双方谈的是同一事件，关注重点也可能很难协调。此外，历史学家会怎样记录对方的回答？选择保留哪些内容、怎样整理和转述，本身也带有主观性，很难保证这些选择能够摆脱时代的局限。第九章中，Thongchai承认自己作为昔日学生领袖的身份影响了访谈：有人认出他后拒绝受访，也有人因此向他表达了可能不会告诉其他采访者的想法。〔5〕采访者如果换成另一个人，得到的回答可能就会很不一样。
paragraphs.english: The second question in our class group discussion was: how should historians study the meanings and limits of existing historical knowledge? In my view, it is difficult to answer this question only by interviewing people from that time. First, people's perspectives change over time. The questions a historian prepares before an interview may not be the ones the interviewee considers important. Even when both are discussing the same event, it may be hard to find a common focus. Also, how will the historian record the answers? Choosing what to keep and how to organize and retell it is itself subjective. It is hard to be sure that these choices can escape the limits of the historian's own time. In chapter 9, Thongchai acknowledges that his identity as a former student leader affected his interviews. Some people refused to be interviewed after recognizing him. Others shared thoughts with him that they might not have shared with another interviewer.〔5〕 A different interviewer might have received very different answers.

paragraphs.chinese: 这也让我想到，普通人和历史学者的记忆，受到社会、个人等因素的影响会有区别吗？历史学家有核查和比较材料的方法，但我不觉得，这就使他们能够完全离开自己的处境。Thongchai既是亲历者，也是研究者。他可以接近某些记忆，也有自己不愿意继续理解昔日对手的时候。他把这些限制写了出来，但我还是想问：如果提问和记录都受到自己的立场影响，历史学家怎样发现那些自己没有意识到的选择？这让我更在意受访者说了什么，和历史学家最后写下了什么之间的差别。
paragraphs.english: This also makes me wonder: are the memories of ordinary people and historians affected differently by social and personal factors? Historians have methods for checking and comparing sources, but I do not think this allows them to step completely outside their own circumstances. Thongchai is both a participant and a researcher. He can gain access to certain memories, but at times he does not want to understand his former opponents more deeply. He writes about these limits, but I still want to ask: if historians' questions and records are shaped by their own perspectives, how can they notice choices they do not realize they are making? This makes me pay more attention to the difference between what an interviewee says and what the historian finally writes down.

paragraphs.chinese: 我想，不是所有的“沉默”都愿意成为“沉默”。很多没有被说出的经历，其实是渴望被表达、被记录的。为了表达这些沉默而进行的纪念、搜集和讲述，又会留下新的记录，产生新的历史声音。但想到当事人时，我又很难认为，记录得越完整、公开得越多就一定越好。书中一位父亲的寻子回忆录没有结尾。Thongchai请他续写时，才意识到这个要求可能带来难以承受的痛苦。〔6〕对研究者来说，这是还没有写完的材料；对这位父亲来说，没有结尾却可能与他不愿放弃的希望有关。这样一来，研究者想弄清楚的事情，就未必是当事人愿意继续讲述的事情。
paragraphs.english: I think some “silences” do not want to remain silent. Many unspoken experiences are waiting to be expressed and recorded. Efforts to express these silences through commemoration, collecting materials and telling stories also leave new records and create new historical voices. But when I think about those involved, I find it hard to say that more complete records and more public information are always better. In the book, a father's account of his search for his son has no ending. When Thongchai asked the father to continue writing, he realized that the request might cause unbearable pain.〔6〕 For a researcher, this is an unfinished source. For the father, however, the lack of an ending may be linked to a hope he does not want to give up. What the researcher wants to find out may therefore be something the person involved is unwilling to discuss further.

paragraphs.chinese: 阅读时，我也想到了梨泰院踩踏事件受害者的后续记录。这看起来与书中的政治暴力差别很大，但它让我想到的，也是当事人是否愿意重新回忆的问题。对事件的记录、对责任的认定，即使有必要，也可能让一些当事人重新面对自己不愿回忆的经过。我担心的是，研究者想保存真相的愿望，会不会把这部分痛苦看得太轻？课堂上一位同学反省，出于善意劝经历战争伤痛的人“放下”，也可能使他们沉默。我觉得这和我的担忧是相通的：要求一个人说出来，或者要求他不再说，都可能没有充分考虑他自己的意愿。尊重当事人的选择很重要，但如果因此不再追问事件，似乎又可能使一些责任继续被回避。这也是我觉得很难处理的地方。
paragraphs.english: While reading, I also thought about efforts to record the experiences of victims of the Itaewon crowd crush after the event. This event seems very different from the political violence in the book, but it raises the same question for me: are those involved willing to recall those experiences again? Documenting an event and establishing responsibility may be necessary, but they may also make some people face experiences they do not want to recall. My concern is whether a researcher's wish to preserve the truth could lead them to underestimate this pain. In class, a classmate reflected that telling people who had suffered from war to “move on” could silence them, even if it was meant kindly. I think this connects with my concern. Asking someone to speak, or asking them to stop speaking, may fail to consider their own wishes fully. Respecting their choices is important. But if this means no longer asking questions about the event, questions about responsibility may continue to be avoided. This is also something I find difficult to deal with.

paragraphs.chinese: 我还不能回答，档案工作是否应该始终以尽可能公开历史真相为目标。但我仍然认为，个人记忆没有得到集体认可，不等于它没有意义；当事人没有讲述，也不等于这段过去已经被遗忘。记录者的立场和当事人的选择，会怎样影响最后留下的历史？这仍是我想继续思考的问题。
paragraphs.english: I still cannot say whether archival work should always aim to make as much of the truth about the past public as possible. But I still think that a personal memory does not become meaningless simply because it has not gained collective recognition. Nor does a person's silence mean that this past has been forgotten. How do the perspectives of those making records and the choices of those involved affect the history that is left behind? This is a question I want to keep thinking about.
